```{=html}
<!--
  THE REPORTING SURFACE, REDRAWN. Included by slides.qmd via {{< include >}}.

  This slide can never use a real capture and that is not a stylistic choice.
  The 11 August 2026 screens carry real citizen names, mobile numbers, email
  addresses and home addresses, and the source document is marked internal, not
  for circulation. So the left panel is drawn in CSS with invented numbers and
  no place names -- office TYPES only, never a named office -- and it is labelled
  as an illustration on its own header, the same rule the desk card follows.

  What is NOT invented is the shape: counts by office and status, a disposal
  percentage over filings, and no time-related field anywhere on the screen.
  That is the finding (Q0.1, Q0.2, Figures B.19-B.20), and it is scoped to the
  CM Grievance Cell in the source line on the slide.

  The right panel is checkable rather than rhetorical: every field names the
  actual column in janasunani/db/models.py that already holds it. The argument
  is not "you should collect more". It is "you already have this".

  Reveal fragments do the reveal. `.rg-f` overrides reveal's default hide so the
  fields start visible-but-grey and light maroon as they are stepped through --
  an absence you can see going from absent to present. No custom JS: if reveal
  never fires, every field simply stays in its grey state and the slide still
  reads correctly.
-->
<div class="repgap">
  <div class="rg-panel rg-today">
    <div class="rg-head">Pendency report &middot; illustration, redrawn, not a capture</div>
    <table class="rg-table">
      <colgroup>
        <col style="width:34%"><col style="width:15%"><col style="width:19%">
        <col style="width:16%"><col style="width:16%">
      </colgroup>
      <thead>
        <tr><th>Office</th><th>Total</th><th>Resolved</th><th>Pending</th><th>Disposal</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Collector</td><td>4,812</td><td>4,166</td><td>646</td><td>86.6</td></tr>
        <tr><td>BDO</td><td>1,340</td><td>1,102</td><td>238</td><td>82.2</td></tr>
        <tr><td>EE, RWSS</td><td>918</td><td>705</td><td>213</td><td>76.8</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Tahasildar</td><td>734</td><td>651</td><td>83</td><td>88.7</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Sub-Collector</td><td>402</td><td>318</td><td>84</td><td>79.1</td></tr>
        <!-- The columns add up and 6,942/8,206 really is 84.6%. Someone in the
             room will check, and an illustration that fails arithmetic costs
             more credibility than it saves effort. -->
        <tr class="rg-total"><td>Total</td><td>8,206</td><td>6,942</td><td>1,264</td><td>84.6</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
    <div class="rg-formula">Disposal rate = (Resolve / Total) &times; 100</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rg-panel rg-missing">
    <div class="rg-head">Already recorded &middot; on no report</div>
    <div class="rg-fields">
      <span class="fragment rg-f"><b>Median age of a pending case</b><i>created_on</i></span>
      <span class="fragment rg-f"><b>Time to first action</b><i>assigned_on</i></span>
      <span class="fragment rg-f"><b>What it is about</b><i>category, subcategory</i></span>
      <span class="fragment rg-f"><b>Where</b><i>district, block</i></span>
      <span class="fragment rg-f"><b>How it was filed</b><i>mode</i></span>
      <span class="fragment rg-f"><b>Who filed</b><i>petitioner_gender</i></span>
      <span class="fragment rg-f"><b>Whether the citizen benefited</b><i>benefitted</i></span>
    </div>
    <div class="rg-foot">Every one of these is a column the portal already writes.
    None of them reaches a report.</div>
  </div>
</div>
```
